title: Steward Incident Lifecycle, Executive Briefing, and Status Templates
author: Priya Nair
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines the Steward incident lifecycle for high-impact degradations and provides a concise executive briefing workflow plus ready-to-use status page and customer communication templates. It combines operational runbook steps, evidence collection requirements for postmortems, on-call rotation expectations during major incidents, and a game-day script for validating the steward flow.

Scope:
- Applies to production-facing services in the inference stack (API gateway, router, runtime, cache/kv, scheduler).
- Intended for incidents that: breach an SLO for >15 minutes, affect >5% of requests, or trigger enterprise customer SLA risk.
- Does NOT replace service-specific runbooks; treat this as the cross-service coordination layer.

Goals:
1) Restore user-visible service quickly while preserving evidence for post-incident review and compliance.
2) Keep executives and customers informed with consistent, tiered messaging.
3) Capture actionable follow-ups and assign stewards for remediation and verification.

Roles and responsibilities:
- Incident Steward (primary): owns the lifecycle, status cadence, and exec brief. Typically an on-call senior SRE or service owner.
- Bridge Operator: facilitates the incident bridge and customer-facing updates.
- Triage Owners: component specialists (API, runtime, cache) who run runbook steps.
- Evidence Custodian: collects logs, spans, replay traces, and cost/credit decisions for audit.
- Escalation Liaisons: Legal/Compliance/Security when customer data or regulatory scope is implicated.

Incident lifecycle (numbered steps):
1) Detection & Acknowledge (0-5 minutes):
   - Pager triggers. First responder posts acknowledgement in the bridge.
   - If p95 latency > 350ms or errors > 3% sustained for 5m, auto-escalate to Steward.
2) Rapid Triage (5-15 minutes):
   - Identify blast radius (services, regions, customer tiers).
   - Run quick checks: infra health (kubectl get pods -n redwood), queue depths, KV cache evictions.
   - If degraded model quality suspected, run golden-prompt sanity check against current model version.
3) Containment (15-45 minutes):
   - Apply throttles, route to fallbacks, or enable cache bypass depending on failure mode.
   - If noisy neighbor suspected, throttle tenant at ingress and notify billing.
4) Stabilization (45-120 minutes):
   - Execute targeted rollbacks, model variant fallback, or scale dedicated pools.
   - Monitor SLO burn; if burn > 10% within the hour, prepare customer notice.
5) Restore & Verify (120+ minutes):
   - Validate with synthetic traffic and key customer prompts, collect traces.
   - Confirm metrics returned to normal for a sustained window (30 minutes p95 within threshold).
6) Close & Postmortem (within 72 hours):
   - Steward files post-incident summary, evidence artifacts, and action items.
   - Mandatory 1-week follow-up on remediation progress.

Runbook snippets (common commands and checks):
- API health: curl -sSf https://health.redwood.internal/api | jq .status
- Pod status: kubectl get pods -n redwood -l service=inference -o wide
- Eviction checks (Redis): redis-cli -h cache-01 INFO ALL | grep evicted_key
- Golden prompt quality test (example): python tools/golden_check.py --model current --batch 20 --prompts tests/golden_prompts.json

SLO thresholds (examples):
- p95 latency (inference API): 350ms
- error rate: <1% overall; tiered customer impact: >3% triggers steward
- availability: 99.9% monthly for core endpoints

Evidence collection checklist (must be attached to postmortem):
- Alert timeline and all pager entries (timestamped).
- Bridge transcript and list of attendees.
- Traces spanning the incident start to restore + 20 minutes.
- Sample request/response pairs (anonymized) for affected customers.
- Configuration diffs (deploys, infra changes) in the 60m prior.

Executive briefing template (short format — 3 bullets):
- Impact: what services/customers and estimated percent of traffic affected.
- Current status: containment steps taken and progress toward SLO.
- Next steps & ETA: remediation actions, timeline, and who owns follow-up.

Status page templates (tiered):
Initial (first 30–60 min):
- Title: Service degradation affecting inference latency
- Body: We are investigating elevated latency impacting a subset of inference requests. Some customers may experience slower responses. Our engineers are actively triaging. Updates every 30 minutes.

Customer-impacting update (after containment):
- Title: Incident update — partial mitigation in place
- Body: We have applied a mitigation that reduced the error rate and restored a portion of traffic. Affected customers: enterprise tier (IDs redacted). Expected full restoration: ~2 hours. We will follow up with a detailed post-incident summary.

Resolved (final):
- Title: Incident resolved — root cause & next steps forthcoming
- Body: The issue is resolved and full service has been restored. We will publish a post-incident report and coordinate any remediation work with impacted customers within 7 business days.

Customer comms style guide (dos/don’ts):
- Do: Be transparent, include timelines/ETAs, and use plain language for non-technical stakeholders.
- Don’t: Speculate about root cause before evidence; don’t promise credits before case assessment.

Postmortem template (required sections):
- Summary: one-paragraph timeline and impact metrics.
- Timeline: minute-level annotated timeline with key actions.
- Root cause & contributing factors: technical explanation and system context.
- Actions: short-term mitigations and long-term fixes with owners and target dates.
- Evidence: links to traces/logs/config diffs.
- Customer communication log: messages sent and links to status page updates.

On-call rotation & steward handoff rules:
- Steward role is assigned to the most senior on-call or on-call lead; if rotation is junior, escalate immediately to on-call lead.
- Handoffs must include: current hypothesis, actions taken, remaining risks, and outstanding owner for customer comms.
- During major incidents, extend rotations to 12-hour shifts for continuity when needed.

Game-day scenario (90-minute exercise):
1) Trigger: synthetic KV cache eviction cascade simulation.
2) Objective: validate Steward detection, exec-brief pipeline, and status page cadence.
3) Steps:
   - 00:00 — Inject cache eviction event in staging that mirrors production traffic.
   - 00:05 — Pager triggers: first responder verifies and posts to the bridge.
   - 00:15 — Steward declares incident, posts initial status page message and notifies PM/CS.
   - 00:45 — Apply planned mitigation (model fallback).
   - 01:15 — Restore service and practice postmortem drafting.
4) Success criteria: initial detection within 10 minutes, status page message posted within 20 minutes, postmortem skeleton created by 90 minutes.

Credit and SLA guidance:
- Credits are considered when SLA breach confirmed and impact > 1% of a customer’s traffic for >30 minutes.
- Steward coordinates with Finance and Sales on credit decisions; no unilateral credit promises on the bridge.

Escalation to Legal & Compliance:
- Immediately loop legal if PII exposure is suspected, or if customers indicate regulatory obligations (e.g., data residency breach).
- Evidence Custodian must preserve raw logs and avoid automatic redaction until advised.

Appendix: quick artifacts and snippets
- Minimal postmortem checklist (tick boxes): Incident ID, Steward, Start/End, Impact %, Evidence links, Actions, Owner signoff.
- Sample bridge message (initial):
   "Incident ID: INC-2026-0391 — A subset of inference requests are experiencing elevated latency. Engineers triaging; next update in 30m. Steward: Priya Nair."
- Sample executive brief (slack/email, 1–3 lines):
   "Status: Partial degradation impacting inference p95. Containment underway via model fallback; expected restoration in ~90 mins. Stewarding: Priya Nair."

Related pages and next rev notes:
- This document should be reviewed after every major incident and during the quarterly game-day schedule. Next formal review: 2026-06-01.

Owner: eng-sre (incident stewardship working group).

End of document.
